links.outcome: Clinical alignment, uncertainty preservation, faithfulness and omission of LLM summaries with versus without grounding constraints
links.effect: Explicit grounding constraints consistently improved clinical alignment, mainly by improving uncertainty preservation. Faithfulness against retrieved evidence was generally preserved or improved. Effects on omission were model-dependent.
links.quote: Across three LLMs and 4,500 generated summaries, explicit grounding constraints consistently improve clinical alignment, particularly by improving uncertainty preservation and, once faithfulness is evaluated against retrieved evidence, generally preserving or improving faithfulness, while effects on omission remain model-dependent.

links.outcome: Readability and medical terminology of grounded patient-facing summaries
links.effect: Improved clinical alignment came at the cost of increased reading difficulty and more medical terminology.
links.quote: We also find that improved clinical alignment comes at the cost of increased reading difficulty and medical terminology.

screen.reason: Evaluates explicit grounding constraints and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) added to LLMs to prevent semantic drift and preserve clinical alignment/uncertainty in patient-facing health summaries.
